name: Queen Mira Valen
playstyle: Court politics, secrets, and the keeping of Caerlyn.
summary: Widow of King Erol. You have ruled beside him for thirty-one years and the court already knows your hand. The crown is in the room with you. So is the suspicion that you helped him die.
hint: You begin inside Castle Caerlyn. Hold the story of Erol's death, the seal, and the Guard. Legitimacy is the thing you do not have.
strengths: Knows who lies for a living
weaknesses: No royal blood of her own

opening_news: The bells of Castle Caerlyn rang before sunrise.
The court has been told King Erol died peacefully. Few believe it.
The Queen's Guard holds the inner doors.

biography: Mira Edevane grew up in a house rich in books and poor in influence. At twenty-three she married Erol, already a king, and learned that affection offered no protection from succession politics. Their pregnancies ended in loss; courtiers made her grief an accusation. She answered by learning every appointment, grain contract and diplomatic debt Erol preferred to leave to others. For thirty-one years she governed from beside his chair, although no writ named her ruler. Her forty-eight guards can secure a bedchamber, not a kingdom. Erol's death has made the work of her lifetime look like theft. She wants the right to finish it. Her greatest danger is the habit of believing that people can be protected only when she controls what they know.
motto: I have kept this kingdom alive.

name: Ethan Valen
playstyle: A name people still trust, an exile's empty purse, and the question of what power will make of you.
hint: You are on the west road with a few men who never accepted the exile. Old regiments still whisper your name. You do not command them yet, and you hold no land.
strengths: A handful of loyal men, and whispers in the old companies
weaknesses: No land, no tax, and almost no coin

opening_news: A wagoner on the west road says the king is dead.
A handful of men still ride at your stirrup. They are loyal. They are not an army.
In the old regiments your name is a whisper, not a banner.

biography: At nineteen Ethan chose a soldier's commission over a place at his brother's table. Eleven years commanding the Queen's Guard taught him to settle disputes before drawing a sword, and to remember the names of the people who carried his baggage. Garran Vale was one of his youngest pupils. Six years ago a private encounter in Mira's rooms ended in an accusation of sexual assault. Ethan denied the charge; Erol allowed exile in place of execution. The dispute remains unresolved. Since then Ethan has repaired fences, escorted caravans and taken wages as a guard under borrowed names. Ordinary hardship has changed him more than he admits. His brother's death offers him a claim by blood, but returning also exposes the people who sheltered him. He must decide whether restoring his name matters more than sparing the kingdom another family war.
motto: A name must be worth returning to.
summary: At nineteen Ethan chose a soldier's commission over a place at his brother's table.

name: Arlo
playstyle: A mystery in a stable. Proof first. A crown only if you decide the proof means you should wear it.
hint: You are not a claimant yet. Lord Tomas has called you inside. Do not promise the realm anything until you know what the letter is.
strengths: A life lived among ordinary people
weaknesses: No title, no army, no name that matters

opening_news: Lord Tomas has called you in from the stables.
A sealed letter waits on the table. The wax is royal.
The annual remittance from Caerlyn will not be renewed.

biography: Lysa, a servant at the royal hunting lodge, died giving birth to Arlo. Tomas and Evelyne Maren raised him alongside their children, taught him letters and riding, and never quite explained why he had no place in the family register. At twenty-four he manages the estate's finest horses. He knows which farmers can lend a cart, which farriers will work on credit, and how hunger turns good animals dangerous. An elderly tutor called Master Ren visited him from the age of thirteen, bringing history and chess rather than answers about his birth. Now a royal letter waits in Tomas's counting room, and twenty-three years of annual payments have ended. If Arlo is Erol's son, proving it will still not make him legitimate. He must build a future that is more than repayment for being hidden.
motto: Blood is a beginning, not an answer.
summary: Lysa, a servant at the royal hunting lodge, died giving birth to Arlo.

name: Lord Alistair Storm
playstyle: An army, a fortress, and the argument that Nezrel will die without a hard hand.
hint: The northern host is already mustered, and Stormhold already answers to you. Marching is the easy part. Being accepted afterwards is the campaign.
weaknesses: The south already sees a conqueror

opening_news: Messengers from the south confirm that Erol is dead.
Eight thousand soldiers can move when you say the word.
Queen Mira has not answered the offer of marriage.

biography: Alistair inherited Stormhold at seventeen when his father died fighting raiders beyond the northern passes. His first winter was an exercise in counting: mine deaths, lost wagons, levy households and the grain left before spring. He built roads, regular pay and harsh courts because disorder had already killed people he knew. Nearly eight thousand soldiers now answer to him, but his belief in order has hardened into distrust of anyone who refuses his solution. House Storm's antiquity gives him pride, not a Valen claim. He has offered Mira marriage and threatened to march if she refuses. Southern people hear a conqueror; northern families hear the man who kept the passes open. The crisis may teach him that a defended kingdom is not the same thing as an obedient one.
motto: A realm must be held before it can be loved.
summary: Alistair inherited Stormhold at seventeen when his father died fighting raiders beyond the northern passes.
